content.text: {"predictors": [{"name": "Inventory Growth Divergence", "construction": "Compute year-over-year growth in raw-materials plus work-in-process inventory (Compustat inventory detail) minus year-over-year growth in sales. Rank firms cross-sectionally each June using the most recent fiscal-year data.", "rationale": "Rising input inventories not matched by sales signal weakening demand and overinvestment, which precede lower future earnings and returns.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (inventory growth below sales growth)"}, {"name": "Accrual-to-Cashflow Quality", "construction": "Compute (net income minus operating cash proxy) scaled by average total assets, where operating cash proxy = net income minus change in non-cash working capital plus depreciation, using Compustat balance-sheet and income-statement items. Sort firms into deciles each June.", "rationale": "Earnings driven by accruals rather than cash are less persistent and tend to reverse, so high-accrual firms subsequently underperform.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (low accrual component of earnings)"}, {"name": "Capital Expenditure Intensity Shock", "construction": "Compute current-year capex scaled by total assets minus the trailing three-year average of the same ratio, using Compustat capital expenditure and asset data. Rank cross-sectionally each June.", "rationale": "Abnormal spikes in investment reflect empire-building and diminishing marginal returns on capital, leading to lower subsequent stock returns.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (below-average investment shocks)"}, {"name": "Gross Margin Trend", "construction": "Compute the change in gross margin (sales minus cost of goods sold, divided by sales) from the prior fiscal year to the current fiscal year using Compustat. Rank firms each June.", "rationale": "Improving gross margins indicate strengthening competitive position and pricing power that the market underreacts to, forecasting higher returns.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure (improving gross margins)"}, {"name": "Dividend Initiation Momentum", "construction": "Flag firms that paid a cash dividend in the most recent CRSP distribution history but paid none in the prior 12 months; among dividend payers, also compute trailing 12-month dividend growth. Portfolio of initiators/high growers vs. non-payers.", "rationale": "Dividend initiations and increases credibly signal managerial confidence in sustainable cash flows, which the market prices with a lag.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure (initiators and strong dividend growers)"}, {"name": "Share Issuance Contraction", "construction": "Compute the log change in split-adjusted shares outstanding over the prior 12 months using CRSP shares outstanding and adjustment factors. Rank firms cross-sectionally each month.", "rationale": "Net share issuance dilutes existing holders and often coincides with overvaluation and market-timing by managers; firms shrinking share count outperform.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (share count contraction/repurchasers)"}, {"name": "Volatility of Turnover", "construction": "Compute the coefficient of variation of monthly share turnover (CRSP volume divided by shares outstanding) over the trailing 12 months. Sort firms into deciles each month.", "rationale": "Unstable trading intensity reflects heterogeneous, sentiment-driven investor demand and higher mispricing risk, associated with lower future returns.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (stable turnover)"}, {"name": "Earnings Announcement Return Clustering", "construction": "Sum the market-adjusted CRSP returns over the three-day windows around the last four quarterly earnings announcement dates (from Compustat report dates). Rank firms each quarter.", "rationale": "Positive cumulative reactions to recent earnings news reflect persistent positive information flow that continues due to underreaction.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure (positive announcement-window returns)"}, {"name": "Asset Turnover Improvement", "construction": "Compute sales divided by average total assets for the current fiscal year minus the same ratio in the prior year, using Compustat. Rank firms cross-sectionally each June.", "rationale": "Rising asset efficiency signals better operating execution and future profitability growth that is not yet fully reflected in prices.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure (improving asset turnover)"}, {"name": "Leverage-Adjusted Profitability", "construction": "Compute operating income before depreciation divided by total assets, then subtract a penalty equal to (total debt / total assets) times a fixed cost-of-debt proxy; use Compustat items. Rank firms each June.", "rationale": "Firms generating high operating returns relative to their debt burden have safer, more sustainable earnings that the market undervalues.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure (high leverage-adjusted profitability)"}]}
